candidates.attacker_control: Not demonstrated for anonymous remote users. The XML documents parsed through this method originate from admin/config-controlled locations: ${dspace.dir}/config/submission-forms*.xml, item-submission.xml, entities.xml, config/registries/*.xml (loaded during DB migration by RegistryUpdater), or CLI-specified files/stdin for structure-builder and registry-loader. An attacker would need to influence or supply one of those XML documents (e.g., a registry/structure XML imported from an untrusted source, or write access to the config directory), and the parsed entity content must be reachable/observable.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: Verified all in-tree callers of getTrustedDocumentBuilder and found none that parse directly attacker-supplied request bodies, so an unauthenticated remote path is not established. Confirmed the sibling hardened paths are intact: getDocumentBuilderFactory() disables DOCTYPE/external general+parameter entities/DTD loading/XInclude (lines 203-219) and getSAXBuilder() disables DOCTYPE/entities (lines 274-291), so the defect is localized to the trusted builder. Confirmed no test references getTrustedDocumentBuilder or PathRestrictedEntityResolver. Confirmed the resolver is never attached anywhere else (only setEntityResolver occurrence in the tree), making the code path dead and the javadoc/behavior mismatch unambiguous.
candidates.impact: Loss of the intended XXE mitigation: local file disclosure (e.g., dspace.cfg / secrets readable by the DSpace process), SSRF against internal services, and potential persistence of fetched entity values when the XML is imported into the registry/metadata tables or rendered in the submission UI. Impact is constrained by the fact that the XML sources are normally admin-controlled, so this is primarily a defense-in-depth regression exploitable where an untrusted XML document can be fed to these components.
candidates.prerequisites: Control over (or ability to trick an operator into importing) an XML file consumed by one of the six callers; a DOCTYPE with an external entity (file:// or http://) in that XML; DSpace process permissions to read the target local file or network reachability to the target host; entity content visible in parsed form, logs, responses or persisted data.
candidates.root_cause: In XMLUtils.getTrustedDocumentBuilder(String... allowedPaths), the configured builder is thrown away: `DocumentBuilder builder = factory.newDocumentBuilder(); builder.setEntityResolver(new PathRestrictedEntityResolver(allowedPaths)); return factory.newDocumentBuilder();` (lines 243-245). The returned builder has no EntityResolver, and the factory comes from getTrustedDocumentBuilderFactory() (lines 191-195), which deliberately sets no DOCTYPE/external-entity features. External entities are therefore resolved without the directory restriction documented in the method javadoc ('If no allowedPaths are passed, then all external entities are rejected') and in the resolver class javadoc.
candidates.title: XXE path restriction bypass: getTrustedDocumentBuilder discards its PathRestrictedEntityResolver
candidates.trace: XMLUtils.getTrustedDocumentBuilder(allowedPaths) -> factory = getTrustedDocumentBuilderFactory() (no external-entity features disabled) -> builder.setEntityResolver(new PathRestrictedEntityResolver(allowedPaths)) on a local variable -> return factory.newDocumentBuilder() (resolver lost) -> callers DCInputsReader.buildInputs (line 130), SubmissionConfigReader (line 175), RegistryImporter (line 54), RegistryLoader (line 271), StructBuilder.loadXML (line 617), InitializeEntities (line 143) parse XML with the unrestricted builder -> `<!ENTITY xxe SYSTEM "file:///...">` (or http URL) is resolved and its contents substituted into the parsed document.
candidates.unverified: End-to-end exploitability in a default deployment is not proven (requires an attacker-influenced XML document in a trusted location). No dynamic parsing, test execution, or file-content verification was performed. Whether this line differs from the upstream/patched DSpace source could not be confirmed offline; the assessment rests on the code contradicting its own security design.
candidates.weakness_type: CWE-611 Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference (XXE)

coverage_summary: Scope: 3301 model-visible files (0 excluded as binary-like, 0 sensitive-name/path exclusions, 0 symlink exclusions, all under the 5 MiB text limit) across dspace-api, dspace-server-webapp, dspace-services, dspace-oai, dspace-rdf, dspace-sword, dspace-swordv2, dspace-iiif and dspace/modules. I inspected the Spring Security configuration and JWT handler, REST permission evaluators, redirect handling (OIDC/ORCID/Shibboleth), bitstream download/content-disposition logic, XML parsing utilities, item import/export and zip extraction, DAO/HQL query construction, storage/bitstore path handling, and external-service clients (OpenAIRE/ORCID/METS/link-checker) using targeted searches and bounded file reads. I did not exhaustively read all 3301 files; coverage of large modules (sword, swordv2, rdf, oai, services, statistics) is partial and driven by security-relevant sink searches.
limitations: No runtime execution, tests, scanners, or exploit payloads were used; findings are source-evidence only.
No git history, diffs, patch metadata, CVE information, or upstream comparison was available, so I cannot prove whether the identified defect is an introduced regression or an upstream issue.
Reachability of the selected finding depends on attacker influence over config-directory/CLI XML files; no unauthenticated remote path was proven.
Binary-like files (none reported by scope filters) and generated/vendored content were not analyzed; test sources were only spot-checked.
Coverage is sampling-based across a large repository; other latent issues may exist in areas not searched (e.g., statistics/Solr, OAI query filters, Sword deposit flows).

rejected_leads.lead: OREIngestionCrosswalk fetches any atom:link href with new URL(...).openStream() and no host allow-list (dspace-api/src/main/java/org/dspace/content/crosswalk/OREIngestionCrosswalk.java, lines 170-186).
rejected_leads.reason: Looks SSRF-like, but this is longstanding design behavior gated behind ORE/package ingestion; I could not establish a reachable, unauthenticated or low-privilege path from the REST/SWORD APIs in this snapshot.

rejected_leads.lead: login.html builds an anchor from the WWW-Authenticate 'location=' value via jQuery .append (dspace-server-webapp/src/main/resources/static/login.html, lines 122-171).
rejected_leads.reason: The header value is generated server-side from authentication-plugin configuration (Oidc/Orcid/Shib loginPageURL), not from request input, so attacker control of the inserted string was not established.

rejected_leads.lead: dspace-api/src/main/java/org/dspace/authority/util/XMLUtils.java convertStreamToXML (lines 139-156) uses a default DocumentBuilderFactory with no XXE hardening.
rejected_leads.reason: No in-tree callers were found for this method, so reachability is absent; weaker than the selected candidate.

rejected_leads.lead: AbstractMETSIngester performs an HTTP GET on a path taken from a METS document (dspace-api/src/main/java/org/dspace/content/packager/AbstractMETSIngester.java, line 1317); BasicLinkChecker and MetadataWebService similarly fetch URLs derived from item metadata/calls.
rejected_leads.reason: These are longstanding, curation/ingest-time features in upstream DSpace rather than an evident regression; no clear privilege boundary crossing was demonstrated, and they were not confirmed reachable by untrusted input.
The zip-slip guards are present and correct in this snapshot (ItemImportServiceImpl lines 1969-1976; SimpleZipContentIngester lines 142-145), so no candidate there.

rejected_leads.lead: Open-redirect validation in OIDC/ORCID/Shibboleth login filters and OidcRestController.
rejected_leads.reason: All four implementations consistently compare Utils.getHostName(redirectUrl) against server/UI/CORS hostnames before sendRedirect; no bypass was identified.

summary: Source review of the DSpace 8.2-SNAPSHOT tree (3301 model-visible files). I traced the strongest distinct, source-evidenced defect to a broken XML security control in dspace-api: XMLUtils.getTrustedDocumentBuilder(...) attaches a PathRestrictedEntityResolver to a locally created DocumentBuilder but then returns a different, freshly created builder, silently discarding the restriction. All six in-tree callers parse XML with the returned builder (submission-forms.xml, item-submission.xml, entities.xml, config/registries/*.xml, structure-builder input), so external entities are resolved without the intended path restriction (CWE-611). Other candidate leads (SSRF surfaces in ORE/METS/BasicLinkChecker, DOM sink in login.html, unused XXE-unsafe helper in authority XMLUtils) were rejected as design-level or non-reachable; only one candidate is submitted per the review cap.
